text:
kevin: Heads up — noticed a spike of low-sev SLO alerts showing up in the console this morning (~120 alerts for one tenant during a deploy window). Paging the oncall and cluttering dashboards. Anyone else seeing this? cc @oncall-team :grimacing:

nadia: Yep, saw it. Mostly `error_rate > threshold` for 1m windows. Dashboard is P99-focused but alerting uses rolling 1m; that mismatch is amplifying noise.

ashley: Is this the new per-tenant notify policy rollout? We changed the default threshold from 0.5% -> 0.2% for dev tenants last week, right?

sam: We did flip that flag (notify.v2.per_tenant_thresholds = true). Also enabled console preview sampling (`sampled=true`) in the UI, but I think sampling didn't backfill into the routing layer. So console shows fewer alerts but notify-service still fans out everything.

kevin: Tracing looks like: ingress -> rule-eval -> fanout to notify-service -> immediate pager. Want to propose a "soft" path where console still surfaces the alert but we don't fan out to paging unless a dedup/noise score > 0.6. Avoids waking people for churn.

ashley: +1. Could be an API shim like:

```
notify.create(alert, {
  route_hint: 'console-only',
  escalate: false
})
```

sam: Implementation note: our notify API currently has `ack_policy` and `escalation_policy`, but no `route_hint`. Adding an enum value is fine, but we'll need a migration plan and feature-flagged rollout.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout flag `notify.v2` enabled on prod-1, prod-2 (2024-11-13T09:12:00Z).

nadia: Short-term: we should consider increasing the evaluation window from 1m -> 5m for "minor" SLOs. That reduces noise and aligns with how dashboards show p95/p99.

kevin: Concern with longer windows is masking short but real outages. Proposal: make it configurable per-route: minor SLOs get 5m + soft-fanout; major SLOs unchanged. Console needs a clear badge ("soft-alert") so people know it didn't escalate.

ashley: UX nit — show a telemetry-derived noise score on each alert card (0.0–1.0). We already compute churn/uniqueness in the telemetry pipeline; exposing it helps triage and justifies soft-fanout.

sam: Backend flow: sampler/telemetry -> compute noise_score -> attach to alert.metadata.noise_score. notify-service consults the noise_score + route_hint to decide fanout. I'll sketch the proto change: `Alert.metadata.noise_score: float` and `FanoutIntent` enum.

nadia: Can we ship a quick fix: patch tenants with >50 alerts/day back to 0.5% threshold? I can run a one-off migration script to reduce churn while we design the API.

kevin: Do that. Also let's open an RFC for the API change + console flag. I'll stub the RFC after lunch and link it here.

ashley: If Nadia runs the tenant patch, log each change and ping SRE. Also add a dashboard card to monitor churn pre/post.

sam: +1. I'll add a feature-flag gate and PR template. For the API enum, I'm thinking: `fanout_intent: ['escalate', 'console_only', 'no_fanout']` — straightforward and explicit.

kevin: Quick checklist: 1) Nadia runs tenant patch 2) Sam adds API enum PR (feature-flagged) 3) Ashley designs soft-alert badge in console 4) Kevin writes RFC and rollout plan. Who owns the dashboard card?

nadia: I can own the dashboard card. Will post the patch PR and dashboard link when done.

ashley: :eyes: thanks — add unit/integration tests around fanout decision logic and a knob in the console to toggle soft-alert visibility for beta users.

sam: Will do. Also we'll need to update docs for oncall playbooks (what to do when a soft-alert is promoted).

kevin: Perfect. I'll open the RFC and channel the plan into the postmortem flow if this reoccurs. Thanks all.

(Conversation ends)
